newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends sharply stronger on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends sharply stronger on fund buying.

text.p: * The Canada dollar ended exactly one Canadian cent stronger at C$1.3875 (US$0.7207) from Thursday's close of C$1.3975 (US$0.7155) after international funds bought Canadian dollars. * Dealers said the Bank of Canada bought U.S. dollars for Canadian dollars around C$1.3885 (US$0.7202) in an effort to smooth the currency's rise.

Analysts said part of the rush to get back into the Canada dollar was the theory that the currency could not sustain any long-term position outside of a range from C$1.3400 (US$0.7462) to C$1.3800 (US$0.7246).

"The Canadian dollar underwent a sharp technical rebound today," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst for Technical Data. "It got its start from foreign buying of Canadian bonds and then took on a life of its own in Toronto's session."
But Hall said the currency could give back all its gains if U.S. payrolls data for April were higher than expected on Friday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

A Reuter survey of economists forecast on average that payrolls in April rose by 211,000. Any rise greater than that would renew speculation about an interest rate rise from the Federal Reserve next month.
The Canadian dollar has been under increasing pressure since the Fed raised U.S. rates by 25 basis points, widening the spread between short-term U.S. and Canadian interest rates.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2406 marks from 1.2379 on Wednesday and jumped to 91.07 yen from Wednesday's 90.80 yen.
((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
